experiments.purpose: Run all 20 official public cases from the official mysqltest package.
experiments.output: 20/20 PASS including SQL, storage, transaction, crash/restart and vector cases; RESULT PASS.
experiments.interpretation: The current implementation satisfies every public functional assertion, including BIGINT precision, Unicode, float32 storage, filtered TopK, ties by primary key, transaction rollback and restart recovery.

experiments.purpose: Exercise hidden-risk paths not present in the public set: NaN, Infinity, float32 overflow, dimension mismatch, malformed vector, crash after commit and crash inside an uncommitted transaction.
experiments.output: NaN/Infinity/overflow => invalid_vector; [1,2,3] on VECTOR(2) => dimension_mismatch; malformed vector => invalid_vector; after SIGKILL of a committed insert, restart returned the committed rows; after SIGKILL inside BEGIN/DELETE, restart returned the original rows.
experiments.interpretation: Invalid vector errors are structured and the WAL/snapshot recovery preserves committed data while discarding uncommitted changes.

experiments.purpose: Measure the 10,000-row/128-dimension benchmark shape and restart recovery.
experiments.command: python3 perf.py (100 batches of 100 vectors; 20 filtered L2 TopK queries; fresh Engine reload)
experiments.output: load 3.0 s; 20 filtered TopK queries 0.337 s; reload COUNT(*) = 10000.
experiments.interpretation: Append-only insert WAL avoids rewriting a full JSON snapshot per batch. Exact query scans use a cached float32 matrix.

experiments.purpose: Run the official JSONL protocol at the wire level.
experiments.output: startup line is exactly {"type":"ready"}; execute responses preserve numeric ids and emit columns/rows or affected_rows; shutdown emits {"id":N,"ok":true} and exits 0; stdout contains only JSONL.
experiments.interpretation: The process follows the official JSON Lines framing instead of the superseded MySQL/text/READY variants.

experiments.purpose: Build the actual Docker image and run the official protocol checker and all public cases through Docker.
experiments.command: GitHub Actions run 42778867412: docker build -t minivectordb:ci .; protocol_check/run.py --image minivectordb:ci ...
experiments.output: handshake: PASS; all 20 public cases PASS (sql_crud ... transaction_shutdown_rollback); Docker image built from source under --read-only, --network=none, 2 CPU, 2 GiB, 128 PID.
experiments.interpretation: The Dockerfile starts the JSONL program correctly and the official protocol checker passes against the real image.

experiments.purpose: Optimize repeated exact vector scans while retaining official public-case correctness.
experiments.command: local 10K x 128 benchmark and official public runner after patching norm caching
experiments.output: official public cases: 20/20 PASS; 10K benchmark total 9.885 s (insert 4.102 s, query 5.783 s), down from prior local 11.978 s.
experiments.interpretation: The cached norm + matrix-vector distance path removes a large per-query temporary allocation and improves the measured query path without changing public-case results.

experiments.purpose: Validate the optimized engine through the real Linux Docker boundary.
experiments.command: GitHub Actions run 42797438284 (workflow round2-official-check): docker build, official protocol_check handshake, then all public cases
experiments.output: workflow conclusion success; official handshake passed; all 20 official public cases passed in the Ubuntu Docker job.
experiments.interpretation: The same engine content used by the submission passes the official JSONL protocol and public MySQL gate under Linux Docker, not only on the Windows development host.

experiments.purpose: Verify the compiled C++ fastscan path in the real Linux Docker image.
experiments.command: GitHub Actions run 42808556753: docker build, official handshake, all public cases, with MVD_REQUIRE_FASTSCAN=1
experiments.output: workflow conclusion success; the image fails if libfastscan.so is not loadable; official handshake and 20/20 public cases passed.
experiments.interpretation: The native fastscan library was actually loaded and executed by the Linux image; this is not merely the NumPy fallback path.

student_evidence: The student supplied the complete task screenshots, selected MiniVectorDB as the add-on task, and repeatedly required verification rather than unsupported claims.
The student granted computer control and explicitly asked for an official repository/web check, which led to discovery of the official mysqltest package.
The student required that only real tests and evidence be claimed; the earlier guessed MySQL protocol was replaced after official STDIO_PROTOCOL.md was found.
result_evidence: Official public suite output: 20/20 PASS, RESULT PASS.
Invalid vector responses: {'ok': False, 'error': {'code': 'invalid_vector', ...}} for NaN/Infinity/overflow; dimension_mismatch for wrong dimension.
Crash recovery: committed rows survived SIGKILL; an uncommitted DELETE did not survive SIGKILL.
Performance shape: 10,000 rows loaded in 3.0 s; 20 filtered TopK queries in 0.337 s; reload COUNT(*) = 10000.
Post-optimization official public suite: 20/20 PASS. Local 10K x 128 benchmark: 9.885 s total (insert 4.102 s, query 5.783 s), compared with 11.978 s before the norm-cache change.
Linux Docker CI run 42797438284 succeeded for the optimized engine: docker build, official handshake, and all 20 official public cases passed.
Linux Docker CI run 42808556753 required MVD_REQUIRE_FASTSCAN=1, loaded libfastscan.so, and passed the official handshake plus all 20 public cases.
retrospective: The first protocol guess (MySQL wire) was wrong. Reading the official STDIO_PROTOCOL.md changed the design to JSON Lines with a ready object and per-request ids.
The public package is genuinely useful: it exposed the exact response schema, row/column comparison, 1e-5 float tolerance, restart directives and vector tie rules.
The engine keeps exact TopK semantics; for the visible tests this is sufficient and guarantees recall for ANN-mode requests, at the cost of performance ranking.
WAL is used only for insert batches; schema changes, updates and deletes write a full atomic snapshot. This keeps the benchmark load fast while preserving crash safety.
limitations: Only the 20 public cases were available; the 9 formal hidden cases are not published and were not run.
ANN is served by exact search; small ANN cases return exact results, but large ANN latency/recall ranking is not measured.
Data larger than memory is not fully disk-streamed; the visible and benchmark shapes fit in memory.
